A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SWE-Search study and provide readable methods, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–L. The appendix text and rendered content match after accounting for page numbers, supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original SWE-bench Lite experiments across five models, qualitative case studies, and appendix analyses of value estimation, costs, and compute-matched performance.

after.justification: v6 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and the appendices. Their retention from v4 does not change their status as original empirical results.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 retain the same action agent, numerical and textual value feedback, modified UCT search, and discriminator debate. The appendix prompts are unchanged; the Figure 4a correction does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 300 SWE-bench Lite instances and repository-level issue-resolution task. The repository-specific analyses are also retained, with no added dataset, domain, or test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same Moatless-v0.0.2 and Moatless-Adapted comparisons, and Appendix J retains the same compute-matched baselines. The added Brown et al. citation is not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The five main models, Pass@1 and Pass@5 metrics, 100-iteration search limit, and three-expansion experimental setting remain unchanged. Appendix C's defaults and Appendix J's comparison procedure are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing state-specific-prompt case study in Figure 4a is locally corrected by exchanging the feedback explanations associated with rewards 0 and 75 and shortening the positive explanation. No new experiment is established; the remaining feedback, scaling, solution-selection, and appendix analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 8 retains the same standard-deviation error bars, and Appendix J retains the same five-run baseline description. No uncertainty-reporting practice or run count changes. The new related-work statement about sampling variance does not report uncertainty for this study.

E6.justification: Figure 4a changes the reported qualitative feedback-to-reward pairings: v4 pairs the positive explanation with 0 and the critical explanation with 75; v6 pairs them with 75 and 0, respectively. Numerical benchmark scores, quantitative plots, costs, and appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, history-dependent value-function definition, modified UCT equations, and selection rule are retained. No mathematical assumption, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract foregrounds inference-time scaling without larger models or additional training data, restating the argument already developed in v4 Sections 4.2 and 5. The multi-agent MCTS contribution and reported 23% relative improvement remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of feedback, flexible transitions, search scaling, discriminator selection, and model complementarity remain unchanged. The same solution-selection limitations and future research directions are retained.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, hyperparameters, test execution details, prompts, code links, demo information, and availability statements are unchanged. Appendices A–C and G–L provide the same reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the references add Brown et al. (2024), Large Language Monkeys, with a statement about variability under repeated trajectory sampling. This is a limited addition to the research context; the existing positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v6 rewrites part of the abstract, removes redundant architecture summaries from the introduction and methodology overview, and shortens the benchmark description. It also adds acknowledgments. The overall section organization remains stable.

P2.justification: Figure 4a's feedback panels are edited, Figure 5 is reduced in size, and tables and surrounding text are repositioned through reflow. The author block is adjusted. No figure or table is added or removed, and appendix displays are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v6 corrects the explanation/reward mismatch in Figure 4a and removes repetitive overview prose, modestly improving internal consistency and readability. The experimental and theoretical support remains unchanged, and Figure 4a's caption still has confusing left/right wording. The gains are therefore limited.
